provisions.label: UPSC face authentication
provisions.title: UPSC face authentication: decision-accountability case

caseFields.name: Owner & purpose
caseFields.statement: UPSC with technical support from NeGD; exam identity authentication.

evidence.title: UPSC face authentication implementation
evidence.quote: The face authentication application has been developed and implemented by UPSC with technical support from the National e-Governance Division (NeGD) of Ministry of Electronics and IT.

caseFields.name: Decision role & affected people
caseFields.statement: Mobile identity matching concerns examination candidates; detailed adverse-decision rules are not verified.

evidence.title: UPSC centenary current-status explanation
evidence.quote: Following a pilot at select centres in Gurugram during the NDA & NA (II) and CDS (II) examinations in September 2025, the system was implemented at scale for the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination on 24 May 2026, covering approximately 5.50 lakh candidates.

evidence.title: UPSC face authentication implementation
evidence.quote: It works on any Android smartphone, and invigilators used their own mobile phones for the purpose, thereby reducing hardware costs and easing the logistical burden.

caseFields.name: Deployment & date
caseFields.statement: A September 2025 pilot and scaled use on 24 May 2026 are officially reported, with about 5.50 lakh candidates.

caseFields.name: Procurement & supplier
caseFields.statement: A 2024 PSU tender covered biometrics, facial recognition, QR scans and AI CCTV; the June record describes in-house development. The contract link between them is unverified.

evidence.quote: Tender responses are invited from PSUs for Aadhaar based Fingerprint Authentication/Digital Fingerprint Capturing & Facial Recognition of Candidates, QR Code Scanning of e-Admit Cards and Live AI-based CCTV Surveillance

caseFields.statement: n.a. Awarded supplier, current application budget and contract value were not verified; the tender alone is not an award.

caseFields.statement: Invigilators' Android phones were used. The current data-flow diagram and device/data lifecycle were not verified.

evidence.title: UPSC face authentication implementation

evidence.quote: The time required for a typical face authentication of a candidate is only about 6–8 seconds, which ensured smooth entry and prevented queuing at examination centres.

caseFields.statement: The older tender requires physical photo verification. The current mismatch/technical-failure SOP was not verified.

caseFields.name: Privacy & retention
caseFields.statement: The older tender specifies encrypted cloud holding for at least one year or 30 days after final results, whichever is later. Applying it to the current mobile system is not established.

caseFields.statement: n.a. A system-specific candidate mismatch appeal, deadline and non-biometric fallback were not verified.

caseFields.name: Public outputs & access
caseFields.statement: UPSC publishes implementation descriptions; the actual current failure-handling SOP, audit and test report were not obtained.

provisions.label: SUVAS judicial translation
provisions.title: SUVAS judicial translation: decision-accountability case

caseFields.name: Owner & purpose
caseFields.statement: Supreme Court SUVAS translates judgments and orders to vernacular languages.

evidence.title: Official judicial AI backgrounder
evidence.quote: For this, **SUVAS** **(Supreme Court Vidhik Anuvaad Software)**, an AI-driven translation tool of the Supreme Court, converts English judgments and orders into vernacular languages, enhancing accessibility and regional language use in courts. These translated judgments are hosted on the **e-SCR portal**, significantly expanding public access.

caseFields.name: Decision role & affected people
caseFields.statement: Translation supports people reading court records; it is not itself a decision on the merits of a case.

evidence.title: Official judicial AI backgrounder

evidence.quote: **Supreme Court and High Court AI Translation Committees** oversee quality and constitutional accuracy. AI use remains assistive, with translations reviewed within judicial frameworks to support access to justice.

caseFields.name: Owner & purpose
caseFields.statement: C-DAC Mohali developed the national platform; the parliamentary record describes CDSS functionality.

evidence.title: C-DAC eSanjeevani product description
evidence.quote: eSanjeevani is an indigenous, cloud-native telemedicine platform developed by C-DAC Mohali to address critical healthcare accessibility challenges, including the shortage and uneven distribution of healthcare professionals, limited access to specialist care in rural and remote areas, and gaps in continuity of care.

evidence.title: Lok Sabha telemedicine/CDSS response
evidence.quote: Further, the AI based Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) available on this platform also enables a systematic capture of the diseases symptoms through a detailed patient assistance form, and identification of possible diseases.

caseFields.name: Decision role & affected people
caseFields.statement: Possible diseases and specialist referral support are presented to a doctor at the hub end, affecting patient consultations.

caseFields.name: Deployment & date

evidence.quote: Since its integration in April, 2023 till July, 2026, nearly 30.4 crore eSanjeevani consultations across all States/UTs have been benefited from standardized data capture and nearly 2.13 crore AI based differential diagnosis, ensuring consistency across health and wellness centres.

provisions.summary: Government reporting describes an AI-labelled CDSS integrated in April 2023, with specialist recommendations through a rule engine and differential diagnoses supplied to a doctor.
provisions.interpretation: This is clinician support, not evidence of an autonomous diagnosis. Consultation counts are not safety or diagnostic-accuracy results, and a local CDSS study proposing later integration cannot validate the existing national component.
provisions.caution: Not clinical advice. The records do not establish every CDSS component is machine learning. The privacy policy is undated, and its medical-output carve-out must not be omitted when quoting retention.
provisions.question: Which decision can this system influence, what evidence supports its use, and how can a person obtain human review?

caseFields.name: Owner & purpose
caseFields.statement: Vendor material describes MARVEL adapting CyberEye's CrimeOS with Microsoft technology; the government-authorisation instrument was not verified.

evidence.title: Microsoft CrimeOS customer story
evidence.quote: MARVEL worked to adapt CrimeOS AI, developed by CyberEye - Microsoft AI Partner, to finetune it for compliance with state investigation protocols and further configure it in Marathi for easy adoption across the force.

caseFields.name: Decision role & affected people
caseFields.statement: The reported purpose is complaint processing and investigation assistance; legal consequences and decision boundaries were not verified.

evidence.title: Microsoft MahaCrimeOS feature
evidence.quote: Since April, police there have been using MahaCrimeOS AI, a customized crime investigation platform powered by Microsoft Foundry that helps them process complaints faster and navigate complex data and procedures — all crucial functions for handling cybercrime.

caseFields.name: Deployment & date
caseFields.statement: Sources describe 23 and 25 pilot stations and an announcement to extend to 1,100; a completed station-wise rollout was not verified.

evidence.title: Microsoft MahaCrimeOS feature
evidence.quote: On Dec. 12, 2025, the government of Maharashtra and Microsoft announced that MahaCrimeOS AI will be extended from Nagpur’s 23 police stations to all 1,100 police stations across the state.

evidence.title: Microsoft CrimeOS customer story
evidence.quote: This was successfully deployed as a pilot across 25 police stations in Nagpur Rural, including the Cyber Crime Police Station (CCPS).

evidence.quote: This was successfully deployed as a pilot across 23 police stations in Nagpur Rural, including the cybercrime police stations (CCPS).

caseFields.statement: n.a. Independent error, bias, accuracy and workload evaluations were not verified; vendor anecdotes are not benchmarks.

provisions.summary: Vendor accounts and reporting describe a Nagpur pilot and announced statewide expansion, with inconsistent 23/25-station counts in the reviewed material.
provisions.interpretation: Investigation support can shape what an officer sees and pursues, but claims of speed or statewide scale need operational records. A company story and a repeating news report are not independent performance audits.
provisions.caution: The reviewed corpus did not establish a government procurement award, station-wise completed rollout, performance audit or tool-specific redress procedure. Count differences may reflect dates/denominators; do not choose a convenient number.
